card.title: Coulomb's Law and Force Between Multiple Charges

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Coulomb's Law quantifies the electrostatic force between two stationary point charges as directly proportional to the product of charges and inversely proportional to the square of their separation: F = k|q₁q₂|/r². In vector form, forces obey Newton's third law (F₁₂ = -F₂₁). When immersed in a dielectric medium of relative permittivity κ, the force reduces to F₀/κ.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Coulomb's Law (magnitude): $F = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \frac{|q_1 q_2|}{r^2}$
Coulomb's Law (vector form): $\vec{F}_{12} = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \frac{q_1 q_2}{r^2}\hat{r}_{21} = -\vec{F}_{21}$
Force in dielectric medium: $F_m = \frac{F_0}{\varepsilon_r} = \frac{F_0}{\kappa} = \frac{1}{4\pi\kappa\varepsilon_0} \frac{|q_1 q_2|}{r^2}$

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Adding electrostatic forces as scalar algebraic quantities: Electric forces are vectors! When calculating the net force exerted by multiple charges, one must resolve each pairwise force into Cartesian orthogonal components ($F_x, F_y$) before summing: $F_{net} = \sqrt{(\sum F_x)^2 + (\sum F_y)^2}$.  ·  Ignoring the medium's dielectric screening: In water ($\kappa \approx 80$), the electrostatic force between ions drops to $\frac{1}{80}$ of its vacuum value, explaining why table salt ($NaCl$) spontaneously dissociates into hydrated $Na^+$ and $Cl^-$ ions in water.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Coulomb's law is strictly valid only for stationary point charges in an inertial reference frame. Accelerating charges radiate electromagnetic energy.  ·  Definition of 1 Coulomb: That charge which, when placed in vacuum at a distance of 1 meter from an identical charge, repels it with a force of 9 × 10⁹ N.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Ionic lattice cohesion in minerals: Table salt crystals ($NaCl$) are held together by Coulomb attraction between alternating $Na^+$ cations and $Cl^-$ anions, providing a high melting point of 801 °C.  ·  Atomic electron orbitals: In Bohr's model of the hydrogen atom, the electrostatic Coulomb attraction between the single proton nucleus and orbiting electron ($F = \frac{e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^2}$) provides the required centripetal acceleration ($m v^2 / r$).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Applying Coulomb's law to extended charge distributions at close range: Coulomb's inverse-square formula applies strictly to point charges or non-overlapping spherical charge distributions (via Shell Theorem). At close range, induction distorts charge distribution on real conductors.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Express Coulomb's law in vector notation with positional unit vectors.  ·  Solve problems calculating net force at a polygon vertex using vector components.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Equilibrium between like charges q₁ and q₂ at distance L: Third charge of opposite sign placed at x = L / (√(q₂/q₁) + 1) from q₁ achieves equilibrium.  ·  Ratio of forces in dielectric medium: F_air / F_medium = κ.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Q1. State Coulomb's law in electrostatics. Express it in vector form and show that it satisfies Newton's third law of motion.  ·  Q2. Define the SI unit of electric charge (1 Coulomb) in terms of Coulomb's law.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: State Coulomb's law in vector form and derive the condition for third charge equilibrium along a line joining two point charges (frequent 3-4 mark NEB question).

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Inverse-square law and electrostatic proportionality constant k = 1/(4πε₀).  ·  Coulomb's law in vector form satisfying Newton's third law (central force).  ·  Dielectric screening effect and definition of relative permittivity κ = ε/ε₀.  ·  Principle of linear superposition for discrete charge distributions.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Coulomb's law is an inverse-square central force acting along the line connecting two stationary point charges.  ·  Vector formulation demonstrates mutual symmetry: $\vec{F}_{12} = -\vec{F}_{21}$, fulfilling Newton's third law.  ·  Presence of a dielectric medium with relative permittivity $\kappa > 1$ reduces electrostatic force by a factor of $\kappa$.  ·  The principle of superposition allows independent pairwise summation of forces in multi-charge configurations.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The electrostatic force between two protons inside a nucleus is approximately $10^{36}$ times stronger than the gravitational force between them: $\frac{F_e}{F_g} = \frac{e^2 / (4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^2)}{G m_p^2 / r^2} \approx 1.24 \times 10^{36}$, showing the colossal dominance of electromagnetism over gravity at microscopic scales.  ·  Coulomb's law has been tested experimentally to an accuracy of better than 1 part in $10^{16}$, establishing the inverse power $r^{-(2+\delta)}$ with $|delta| < 10^{-16}$, proving the photon has zero rest mass.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Q3. Two point charges $+4q$ and $+q$ are fixed at a distance $L$ apart. Where should a third charge $Q$ be placed on the line joining them so that the entire system remains in electrostatic equilibrium?  ·  Q4. Explain the principle of linear superposition of electrostatic forces and describe how to calculate the net force on a charge located at the vertex of an equilateral triangle with charges at the other two vertices.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Dissolution in polar solvents: The high dielectric constant of liquid water ($\kappa \approx 80$) reduces ionic attraction by a factor of 80, permitting thermal agitation to break ionic bonds and dissolve salts.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Coulomb's Law of Electrostatics:** Formulated by Charles-Augustin de Coulomb in 1785, the electrostatic force between two stationary point charges is directly proportional to the product of the magnitudes of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them: $F = k \frac{|q_1 q_2|}{r^2}$.…  ·  **Electrostatic Constant & Permittivity of Free Space:** The proportionality constant in vacuum/air is $k = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \approx 8.98755 \times 10^9\,\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2 \approx 9 \times 10^9\,\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2$.…  ·  **Vector Formulation & Newton's Third Law:** In vector notation, the force $\vec{F}_{12}$ exerted on charge $q_1$ by charge $q_2$ located at position vector $\vec{r}_2$ is: $\vec{F}_{12} = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \frac{q_1 q_2}{|\vec{r}_1 - \vec{r}_2|^3} (\vec{r}_1 - \vec{r}_2) = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \frac{q_1 q_2}{r^2} \hat{r}_{21}$.…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Principle of Superposition: $\vec{F}_{net} = \sum_{i=1}^N \vec{F}_i$  ·  Proportionality constant in vacuum: $k = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \approx 8.99 \times 10^9\,\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2$  ·  Earnshaw's theorem establishes that stable electrostatic equilibrium of stationary point charges is impossible without non-electrostatic constraints.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Remember that the permittivity of free space ε₀ has SI units of C²/(N·m²) or F/m, with value 8.854 × 10⁻¹² F/m.  ·  Statement 1: The electrostatic force between two stationary point charges varies inversely with the square of the distance between them.  ·  Statement 2: Electrostatic forces are central forces acting strictly along the straight line joining the centers of two interacting charges.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Statement 3: Electrostatic forces satisfy Newton's third law: the force on charge 1 by charge 2 is equal in magnitude and opposite in direction to the force on charge 2 by charge 1.  ·  Statement 4: The electrostatic force between two charges is independent of the presence of any other surrounding charges.  ·  Statement 5: In any dielectric medium with relative permittivity κ, the electrostatic force between two charges is attenuated by a factor of κ.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Two identical charges in symmetrical polygons: Net electrostatic force at the geometric center of any regular polygon with equal vertices charges is identically ZERO.  ·  Two identical positive point charges $q_1 = q_2 = +2.0\,\mu\text{C}$ are placed at coordinates $(0, 0.3\text{ m})$ and $(0, -0.3\text{ m})$ along the y-axis. A third point charge $q_0 = +4.0\,\mu\text{C}$ is placed on the x-axis at $(0.4\text{ m}, 0)$.…  ·  Determine position and magnitude of a third charge for complete electrostatic equilibrium.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Dielectric Medium & Relative Permittivity:** When point charges are embedded within an insulating medium of permittivity $\varepsilon$, dielectric polarization shields the charges, reducing the net force to $F_m = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon} \frac{|q_1 q_2|}{r^2} = \frac{F_0}{\varepsilon_r} = \frac{F_0}{\kappa}$.…  ·  **Principle of Linear Superposition:** Electrostatic interaction between any pair of charges is completely unaffected by the presence of other surrounding charges.
